Rashi on Nazir 27a:1:1.hebrew: א"ל וליטעמיך הא דתנן רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר כו' - לימא נמי התם דכסתומין דמו, דהא אמרת: בהמה, נסכא וסואר של קורות לאו כמפורשין דמו:
Rashi on Nazir 27a:1:1.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning, that which we learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, etc. - Let us say there as well that they are considered unallocated [funds], for you said [that] an animal, a [silver] bar, and a pile of beams are not considered allocated.

Rashi on Nazir 27a:2:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - לעולם אימא לך: דמעות ולא נסכא, מעות ולא סואר. והא דאמרת "מעות ולא עופות" — התם לא אפשר דליהוו כמפורשין, דהא כתיב בהו "ולקח ועשה", דגלי לך רחמנא דלא ליהוו מפורשין אלא אי בעשיית כהן, אי בלקיחת בעלים. והא נמי דמותבינן לך מבהמה — התם נמי לא אפשר דכסתומין דמו, דמינכרא מילתא דכמפורשין דמו:
Rashi on Nazir 27a:2:1.english: He said to him - Actually, I could tell you that [the tradition teaches:] Money and not a metal bar, money and not a stack [of beams]. And as for that which you said, “[Does it mean] money and not birds?” — there, it is not possible that they should be [considered] allocated, for behold, it is written regarding them: “And he shall take... and he shall sacrifice,” as the Merciful One revealed to you that they do not become allocated except either by the action of the priest or by the acquisition of the owner. And as for that which we also objected to you from [the case of] an animal — there too, it is not possible that they should be considered unallocated, because the matter is distinguishable, so that they are considered as allocated.

Tosafot on Nazir 27a:1:1.hebrew: וליטעמיך הא דתנן רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר הביא שלש בהמות ולא פירש הראוי לחטאת - כגון כבשה — תקריב חטאת; הראויה לעולה, כגון כבש — תקרב עולה; הראוי לשלמים, כגון איל — הראוי לשלמים:
Tosafot on Nazir 27a:1:1.english: "And according to your reasoning, that which we learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: [If] one brought three animals and did not specify, that which is fit for a sin-offering" - Such as a female lamb — is sacrificed as a sin-offering; that which is fit for a burnt-offering, such as a male lamb — is sacrificed as a burnt-offering; that which is fit for a peace-offering, such as a ram — is fit for a peace-offering.

Tosafot on Nazir 27a:1:2.hebrew: ואמאי האמרת [בהמה] לאו כמפורשת דמיא - כלומר, לפי מאי דבעי לאוכוחי מרב חסדא דעופות כסתומין הם, וה"נ בהמה [נימא] כסתומין דמיא ולא כמפורשין — וא"כ יקשה לך: אמאי חשיב להו רשב"ג כמפורשין? וא"ת: ומי דמי? והא בהמה דלעיל דחשיב כסתומים מיירי כגון דהוו ג' פרים, והנהו ודאי הוו כסתומים; אבל אלו בהמות דמיירי כאן רשב"ג מיירי בבהמה דחזו לנזיר, ולכך חשבינן להו כמפורשין! וי"ל: דהכי פירושו — אי אמרת בשלמא כדקאמר רב הונא בבהמות, דהיינו ג' פרים, חשיבי קצת כמפורשין, ולכל הפחות כמפורשין בתערובת, הכא דרשב"ג ניחא, דחושב ג' בהמות הראויים לנזיר כמפורשין לגמרי, כאילו פירש בפיו "זו לחטאת, וזו לעולה, וזו לשלמים"; אלא אי אמרת הג' פרים כסתומין דמיין לגמרי, ה"נ מחמת שהן ראוין לנזיר לא הוה לן למיחשב (בינייהו) לגמרי כמפורשין. וא"ת: ואכתי מאי [פריך? דילמא] רשב"ג איירי כשחזר ופירש הנזיר בפירוש בשעת הקרבה: הי לחטאת, והי לעולה, והי לשלמים? וי"ל: דחדא, לישנא לא משמע הכי, דקתני "הביא ג' בהמות ולא פירש" וכו', ומשמע ליה: הראוי לעולה תקרב לעולה, ומעכשיו — אף קודם הקרבה — יש עליה שם עולה, אף למעול בה, אף אם מתו הבעלים דלמיתה אזלא; ועוד, אי במפורשין בפירוש בשעת הקרבה, צריך למימר?! ומאי קמ"ל רשב"ג? וא"ת: ומאי קס"ד דרב פפא? והא מוכחא מדרב חסדא דבעופות כסתומין דמיין, וה"ה בבהמה! ויש דוחק לומר דרב פפא ס"ל דרב חסדא [בדותא] וליתא, דבכמה דוכתי [מייתי] לדרב חסדא. וצ"ל: דרב פפא ודאי ס"ל דאפילו את"ל דעופות כסתומים דמיין ולא ממעטינן להו ממעות, היינו משום שאין לנו למעט אלא דבר הדומה למעות דלא חזו להקרבה, כגון צפרים דלא חזו לנזיר להקרבה; אבל עופות דחזו גופייהו להקרבה, אין למעטן מהלכה שנתפרש במעות סתומין יפלו לנדבה, והוא הדין דודאי סתומין הוו מעלו לנדבה. ומשני ליה רב שימי, וא"ל: "ולקח... ועשה" אמר רחמנא, בלקיחת בעלים אומר כן; כלומר: ואם לא פירשו הבעלים בשעת הלקיחה הוו כסתומין, והוא הדין דרב הונא דאמר בבהמות דהוו כסתומין לפי שאינו מוכיח מגוף התורים הי חטאת והי עולה, וכן כשהפריש שלשה פרים אין מוכיח מגוף הבהמות כלום הי חטאת והי עולה, הילכך נוכל לומר דהוו כסתומין לגמרי. אבל הכא במתני' דרשב"ג, דקתני "הביא שלש בהמות הראויות", דמוכיח מגוף הבהמה הי לחטאת והי לעולה והי לשלמים — דכבשה לחטאת, שחטאת באה נקבה, וליכא למימר דתקרב עולה, שהעולה בא זכר, דהיינו כבש; וכן איל מפורש בפסחים להדיא דקרב שלמים, וכן כבשה לחטאת, וכן כבש לעולה — הילכך כמפורשין דמו, דאין מפורש גדול מזה! אבל ג' פרים כסתומין דמיין, ולא נאמר: אי ג' פרים הוו כסתומים ה"נ הוו כסתומין — [כך] סבר המקשה:
Tosafot on Nazir 27a:1:2.english: "And why? Didn't you say [an animal] is not treated as allocated?" - That is to say: According to what he wanted to prove from Rav Ḥisda that birds are [treated as] unallocated, so too [let us say that] an animal is treated as unallocated and not as allocated; and if so, it should be difficult for you: Why does Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel consider them allocated? And if you say: Are [the cases] comparable? But the animal [case] above, which was considered unallocated, is dealing with [a case] such as where there were three bulls, and those certainly are unallocated [since they are not fit for a nazirite's offerings]; but these animals that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel deals with here are dealing with animals that are fit for a nazirite, and for this reason we consider them allocated! And one can say: This is the explanation: It is well [and understandable] if you say, as Rav Huna said regarding animals, that where there are three bulls they are considered somewhat allocated, and at the very least as allocated in a mixture — here, [the ruling] of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is well understood, for he considers three animals that are fit for a nazirite as completely allocated, as though he explicitly specified with his mouth: "This is for a sin-offering, this is for a burnt-offering, and this is for a peace-offering." But if you say that the three bulls are treated as completely unallocated, here too, [merely] because they are fit for a nazirite, we should not have considered them (among them) as completely allocated. And if you say: Still, what is [the challenge? Perhaps] Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is dealing with [a case] where the nazirite subsequently specified explicitly at the time of sacrifice which is for a sin-offering, which is for a burnt-offering, and which is for a peace-offering? And one can say: First, the wording does not imply this, as it teaches: "If he brought three animals and did not specify, etc.", and it implies to [the Gemara that] that which is fit for a burnt-offering shall be sacrificed as a burnt-offering, and from now — even prior to sacrifice — it bears the status of a burnt-offering, even to [be liable for] misuse of consecrated property, [and similarly regarding the sin-offering,] even if the owner died, that it goes to death. And furthermore, if [it is dealing with where] they are explicitly specified at the time of sacrifice, does it need to be said?! And what is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaching us? And if you say: And what was Rav Pappa's thinking? But isn't it proven from Rav Ḥisda that with birds they are treated as unallocated, and the same applies to an animal! And it is far-fetched to say that Rav Pappa holds that Rav Ḥisda['s statement is an error] and is not [accepted], since in several places [the Gemara] cites Rav Ḥisda['s teaching]. And one must say: Rav Pappa certainly holds that even if you say that birds are treated as unallocated and we do not exclude them from [the rule of] money, that is because we should only exclude something that is similar to money in that they are not fit for sacrifice, such as birds [tzipporim] which are not fit for a nazirite for sacrifice; but bird offerings [ofot] which are themselves fit for sacrifice, we should not exclude them from the halakha that was explicitly stated regarding unallocated money, [namely that they] shall fall to [the purchase of communal] gift offerings; and the same applies [to birds], that if they were definitely unallocated, they would be offered as a gift offering. And Rav Shimi answered him and said to him: The Merciful One states: "And he shall take... and he shall sacrifice" — He says this regarding the acquisition of the owner; that is to say: and if the owner did not specify at the time of acquisition, they are [treated] as unallocated. And the same applies to [the challenge against] Rav Huna who said regarding animals that they are [treated] as unallocated: because it is not evident from the body of the turtledoves which is a sin-offering and which is a burnt-offering, and likewise when one designated three bulls, nothing is evident from the body of the animals as to which is a sin-offering and which is a burnt-offering; therefore, we can say that they are completely unallocated. However, here in the mishna of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, where it teaches: "If he brought three fit animals," where it is evident from the body of the animal which is for a sin-offering, which is for a burnt-offering, and which is for a peace-offering — for a female lamb is for a sin-offering, as a sin-offering must be female, and one cannot say that it should be sacrificed as a burnt-offering, since a burnt-offering must be male, which is a male lamb; and likewise a ram is explicitly stated in Pesachim to be sacrificed as a peace-offering, and likewise a female lamb for a sin-offering, and likewise a male lamb for a burnt-offering — therefore, they are considered allocated, as there is no greater allocation than this! But three bulls are treated as unallocated, and we do not say: "If three bulls are unallocated, here too they are unallocated" — [so] thought the questioner.
